newsitem.title: USA: St. Pete mayor says city working on race relations.
newsitem.headline: St. Pete mayor says city working on race relations.

text.p: St. Petersburg mayor David Fischer told the U.S. Commission on Civil Rights on Wednesday that efforts were underway to improve living conditions in poor neighbourhoods and overcome racial tension.
The commission is holding a hearing on race relations in St. Petersburg following two outbreaks of unrest.
Rioting erupted in October after the fatal shooting of a black motorist by a white police officer. More violence broke out last month when a grand jury ruled the shooting a justifiable homicide.

Fischer said city authorities were trying to improve living conditions in black neighbourhoods. But his remarks diverged so sharply from testimony the previous day from residents of violence-hit neighbourhoods that hearing chairman Sol Agin recommended the mayor hire an independent assessment.
"You'll build trust," Agin said, "because right now it's not there."
Fischer backed police chief Darrel Stephens, who has come in for harsh criticism from black residents, but he told the commission he wanted an outside investigation of the city police.
Stephens, who spoke after the mayor, was asked to justify his decision to order so-called preemptive arrests before the grand jury's ruling on the October shooting was made public.

He replied: "I felt that under the circumstances, it was a good decision. Turned out that it didn't work out the way we hoped it would, but it was a calculated decision based on what we had been hearing for three weeks."

Stephens admitted he might not make such a decision again and would consult with the mayor rather than act on his own. The hearings opened just as the St. Petersburg Police Union announced a vote of no-confidence in Chief Stephens.

Poor blacks youths in the city have said they face constant harassment from police. Community leaders say that with many of the youths unemployed, frustration and resentment are widespread and the shooting incident fanned the flames.
